notes:
CIRCUIT: a large multi-stage transistor network - 8 BJTs (3 PNP, 5 NPN), 6 resistors, 2 diodes, four one-port supply arrows (+15V, +10V, +3V, +5V, plus one unlabelled arrow at (531,399)) and one GND at bottom right. Rough layout: a +15V rail across the top (y~165) feeding R1 (top left) and Q3 (top right); a mid rail at y~450 carrying R7 (150ohm) and R9 (15kohm) between the R4 node and the +5V node; a common return rail across the bottom (y~855) which is the ground net.

DRAFTER'S CONVENTION ON THIS SHEET (important, and unusually clear): a junction is drawn as a small OPEN CIRCLE on the wire - there are about a dozen of them (S5 (275,303), S6 (278,312), S10/S11 (533,434), S12 (290,445), S13/S14 (819,447), S15 (296,453), S25 (155,588), S26 (564,646), S35/S36 (871,808), S37 (753,819), S39 (689,822), S40 (762,819), S41 (678,825), S42 (226,854), S43 (555,855), S44 (295,855), S45 (565,857), and the one under the +15V arrow at (510,172)). A crossing WITHOUT connection is drawn as a sideways STEP: the wire shifts ~15-20 px to one side, crosses, and steps back. There are exactly two of those on this sheet and neither has a circle.

  n5 = R4 bottom (292,435) through the open circles (290,445)/(296,453), right to R7 left (365,449), and down to Q10 emitter. Terminals 4.1, 7.0, 10.2.
  n6 = mid rail between R7 and R9: R7 right (451,441), open circle (533,434) up to the unlabelled supply arrow #5, R9 left (605,446); the same node runs down to Q11 emitter. Terminals 5.0, 7.1, 9.0, 11.2.

Reached by Q13 collector (233,628), R15 bottom (669,677 via the step at (685,735)), R16 bottom (162,744), Q17 emitter (867,756), Q18 emitter (301,797), Q19 emitter (747,764), Q20 emitter (553,825). Terminals 13.0, 15.1, 16.1, 17.2, 18.2, 19.2, 20.2, 21.0.

JUDGEMENT CALLS:
  S16 (692,455) deg5 CRITICAL -> CROSSING (kept the tracer default; hop_score 23). Verified in the pixels and at 10x zoom: the wire coming down from D6 runs at x~682, steps RIGHT to x~695 just above the mid rail, crosses it, and steps back LEFT to x~680 below it before continuing to D14. No open circle. Read as a junction, D6-bottom and D14-top would merge with the whole +5V mid-rail node (Q3 emitter, +5V arrow, R9 right, Q17 collector) into one 6-terminal net and the two diodes would no longer be a series pair; n7 would disappear.
  S32 (689,734) + S33 (681,736) CRITICAL -> CROSSING, expressed as explicit edge groups because the one drawn crossing was split into two degree-3 sites which junction/crossing alone cannot describe: '32': [[85,89],[86,87,88]] and '33': 'none'. Group 1 (e85 + e89) is the vertical wire - R15's bottom lead comes down at x~669, steps RIGHT to x~687 (inkmap rows 718-732), crosses the horizontal, steps back LEFT to x~669 (rows 738-747) and carries on down to the bottom rail at S39. Group 2 (e86 + e87 + e88) is the horizontal wire at y~735 running from the S26 node (Q11 collector, Q20 collector) rightward to Q19's base. Same step signature as S16, and again no open circle where this drafter puts one at every real junction. This was the tracer's single biggest error: with both sites left as junctions the netlist had one 9-terminal node containing BOTH the base and the emitter of Q19 AND both the collector and the emitter of Q20 - i.e. two transistors short-circuited - which is impossible. Splitting removes those shorts and gives every transistor three distinct nets.
  S26 (564,646) deg3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. An open circle is drawn right on it. Q11 collector, Q20 collector and the run east to Q19's base meet here.
  S29 (735,694) deg3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the wire to Q17's base starts on the D14-to-Q19-collector diagonal. No circle, but a T needs none.
  S39 (689,822) deg5, S42 (226,854) deg8, S44 (295,855) deg3, all CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Each has a clearly drawn open circle; they are the bottom rail's tap points.
  All remaining sites are handwriting ('+15V', '+10V', '15kohm', '150ohm', '50kohm', '50kohm') brushing a wire, or extra skeleton nodes generated by the open circles themselves; left at their defaults and none of them changes a net.

BROKEN-INK MERGES:
  merge ['17.2','19.2'] - the bottom rail runs east from S40 (762,819) to the open circle at (871,812) where Q17's emitter comes down and GND#21 hangs below, but the last stretch of that line is drawn very lightly and the scan has a ~6 px dropout between x=851 and x=857 at y=813 (verified with inkmap at (852,812): solid ink x=830..850, nothing x=851..856, ink resumes x=857). Without the merge the GND net would hold only 2 terminals (Q17 emitter and GND) and the entire bottom return rail - seven transistor/resistor terminals - would float with no ground reference, which is impossible.
  merge ['0.0','1.0'] - the +15V arrow #0's only port candidate was a 6 px stub at (529,131) that is actually part of the handwritten '+' of '+15V'; its real connection is the arrow stem running down out of the annotated box to the open circle at (510,172) on the top rail. No port candidate exists for that stem, so the terminal is pinned to the top rail by merging it with R1's top terminal. Without it net n1 would hold a single terminal.

PIN-ORDER FIXES (3-terminal parts; order is scored, so every transistor was checked at 9x zoom):
  All five NPNs are drawn with the emitter arrow pointing AWAY from the base bar, all three PNPs with the emitter arrow pointing INTO the base bar, and in every PNP here the emitter is the upper lead.
  Q10 BJT-PNP (287,509): base = left lead p0 (253,507); the UPPER lead p1 (294,466) carries the arrowhead pointing down-left into the bar, so it is the EMITTER, and the lower lead p2 (304,550) is the COLLECTOR. The tracer had collector and emitter swapped. Set t0(collector)=p2, t1(base)=p0, t2(emitter)=p1.
  Q11 BJT-PNP (562,538): base = right lead p2 (601,531); upper-left lead p1 (539,494) carries the arrowhead pointing down-right into the bar = EMITTER; lower-left lead p0 (555,580) = COLLECTOR. Set t0=p0, t1=p2, t2=p1.
  Q13 BJT-PNP (222,585): base = left lead p1 (192,582); upper lead p2 (221,541) carries the arrowhead pointing down-left into the bar = EMITTER; lower lead p0 (233,628) = COLLECTOR. Set t0=p0, t1=p1, t2=p2.
  Q3 (805,357), Q17 (842,718), Q18 (314,752), Q19 (734,736), Q20 (535,777) are all NPN and were already correct: base on the odd side (left for Q3/Q17/Q19/Q20... Q18 and Q20 take the base from the right/left respectively as drawn), collector on the lead away from the arrow, emitter on the arrowed lead. Checked each arrowhead individually.

RESULT: 22 components, 15 nets, ERC clean. No class looks wrong. Nothing left unresolved.
